scenes.title: The Hidden Plant Part
narration: Have you ever pulled a carrot out of the soil in your garden?
That orange carrot is actually a very special part of the plant.
It is called a root, and it hides deep underground.

scenes.title: What Do Roots Do
narration: Roots act like tiny straws that soak up water from the dirt.
They also hold the plant tightly so it does not fall over.
Without roots, plants could not drink or stand up tall.

scenes.title: Seeing Roots in Action
narration: Imagine we put a bean seed in a glass of water.
Soon, tiny white threads start to grow out from the seed.
These white threads are the roots reaching out for water.

scenes.title: Roots Are Awesome
narration: Remember, roots are the plant's anchor and its straw.
They keep plants healthy and strong in the ground.
Can you find a plant today and guess how deep its roots go?

scenes.title: Meet the garden hero
narration: Have you ever wondered how water travels from the ground all the way up to the leaves?
Aarav is watering his sunflower in the backyard with his shiny red bucket.
The water disappears into the soil, but the plant drinks it up!

scenes.title: What is a stem
narration: The stem is like a green straw that holds the plant tall.
Inside the stem, there are tiny tubes that act like tunnels.
These tubes carry water and food to every single part of the plant.
Without the stem, the plant would flop over and fall down.

scenes.title: Seeing it in action
narration: Let us try a fun experiment with a white flower and colored water.
Place the flower stem in a glass of water with blue food color.
Wait a few hours and watch the white petals turn blue!
This proves the stem is working hard to pull the water up.

scenes.title: Recap and think
narration: The stem holds the plant up and acts like a water straw.
It moves water from the roots up to the leaves and flowers.
Think about it: do all plants have the same kind of stems?

scenes.title: A Sunny Day Outside
narration: Have you ever wondered why the big peepal tree in our park has so many green leaves?
They are not just for decoration, they are actually working very hard for the tree.
Let us discover how leaves act like tiny kitchens for every plant.

scenes.title: Making Food With Sunlight
narration: First, the leaves catch golden sunlight from the sky to get energy.
Then, they take in water from the roots and air from all around them.
Inside the leaf, sunlight turns the water and air into sweet plant food.

scenes.title: The Mango Tree Example
narration: Think about a mango tree in a garden in Kerala.
The leaves make food that travels down to grow big, juicy mangoes.
Without those green leaves, the tree could not make any fruit for us to eat.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Leaves use sunlight, water, and air to make food for plants to grow.
They also give us fresh air to breathe, which is a wonderful gift.
Think about it, what would happen to plants if the sun stopped shining?

scenes.title: A Garden Surprise
narration: Have you seen colorful flowers in your garden or at the local park?
Arav noticed a tiny bud on a plant yesterday, but today it is open!
How does a tiny seed turn into such a pretty flower?

scenes.title: What Flowers Need
narration: First, the plant needs a cozy home in the soil.
It drinks water from the ground through its long roots.
Then, it catches warm sunlight with its green leaves.
With food and water, the stem grows taller every day.

scenes.title: The Life Cycle
narration: Imagine planting a sunflower seed in a small pot.
Small green leaves sprout and reach for the sky.
Finally, a big yellow flower blooms for all to see.
The flower makes new seeds to start the cycle again.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Flowers
narration: Flowers need water, sunlight, and soil to grow big and strong.
They grow from seeds and help make even more seeds.
Think about it, what would your favorite flower need to grow today?

scenes.title: The Mystery Inside Fruit
narration: Have you ever found a hard little seed inside a tasty mango?
Why do plants hide tiny seeds deep inside their yummy fruits?
Let us discover how these seeds turn into big trees.

scenes.title: How Seeds Start Growing
narration: Every seed is like a tiny sleeping baby plant.
When a seed lands in soil, it needs a drink of water.
The warm sun helps the seed wake up and start growing.
Soon, tiny green roots push deep down into the ground.

scenes.title: From Seed to Tree
narration: Imagine we plant a seed from a sweet guava.
First, a little sprout pokes out of the dirt.
Then, it grows strong branches and many green leaves.
Finally, new flowers bloom and turn into fresh fruit.

scenes.title: Plants are Amazing
narration: Seeds need soil, water, and sun to grow big.
Fruits keep the seeds safe until they are ready.
If you ate an apple today, where could you plant its seeds?

scenes.title: The Curious Little Seed
narration: Have you ever wondered how a tiny seed becomes a giant mango tree in your garden?
Plants cannot walk to the kitchen for a snack, so they make their own food.
Let us discover the magic ingredients plants need to stay happy and healthy.

scenes.title: The Three Main Needs
narration: First, plants need bright sunlight to get energy, just like you need breakfast.
Second, they need water from the soil to help them carry nutrients up.
Third, they need fresh air to breathe through tiny holes in their leaves.

scenes.title: Growing a Marigold Plant
narration: Imagine planting a marigold seed in a small pot of soil at home.
We add a little water and place the pot near the sunny window.
The roots drink water and the green leaves reach up to catch the light.
Soon, a beautiful orange flower blooms for everyone to see.

scenes.title: Recap and Explore
narration: Remember, every plant needs sun, water, and air to grow big and strong.
Take good care of the plants in your balcony to watch them thrive.
Think about it: what would happen to a plant if we kept it in a dark box?

scenes.title: Meeting Our Animal Friends
narration: Have you ever wondered why your pet dog stays home but a tiger lives in the forest?
Today, we are going to learn what makes animals wild or domestic.
Some animals are our friends at home, while others live far away in the wild.

scenes.title: The Meaning of Domestic
narration: Domestic animals live with humans and help us in our daily lives.
We feed them, give them shelter, and they provide us with milk or wool.
Think of the cows grazing in the village fields or a cat in your house.

scenes.title: Life in the Wild
narration: Wild animals find their own food and build their own homes in nature.
They do not need humans to take care of them at all.
Imagine an elephant roaming through a thick forest or a monkey jumping in the trees.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Domestic animals live with us, but wild animals live freely in nature.
Both types of animals are special and important for our world.
Think about it: Why do you think we cannot keep a lion as a pet?

scenes.title: The Big Question
narration: Have you ever wondered where a squirrel or a bird sleeps at night?
Just like you have a cozy house, animals need homes too.
Let us explore where our wild friends hide and rest.

scenes.title: Types of Animal Homes
narration: Birds build soft nests high up in the mango trees.
Rabbits dig deep tunnels underground called burrows to stay safe.
Bees work together to build honeycombs in their busy hives.
Some animals like lions live in caves to stay hidden.

scenes.title: A Squirrel's Home
narration: Look at this squirrel in a park in Delhi.
First, it finds a hole in a sturdy tree trunk.
Next, it fills the hole with dry leaves and grass.
Finally, it has a warm, safe spot for its babies.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Animals use nests, burrows, and caves for safety and sleep.
Every home is perfect for the animal that lives inside.
Think about it: what kind of home would you build if you were an animal?

scenes.title: The Hungry Animal Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered what animals eat for breakfast?
At the park in Delhi, we see cows munching on green grass.
But what about the lions at the zoo?

scenes.title: Three Types of Eaters
narration: Animals are grouped by the food they love to eat.
Herbivores only eat plants like leaves, fruits, and seeds.
Carnivores are hunters that eat meat to stay strong.
Omnivores are special because they eat both plants and meat.

scenes.title: A Day in the Jungle
narration: Look at a small rabbit eating a crunchy carrot.
The rabbit is a herbivore since it only eats plants.
Now see a hungry hawk catching a snack.
The hawk is a carnivore because it eats meat.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Animal Friends
narration: Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat meat, and omnivores eat both.
Every animal has a special diet to help them grow.
Think about it: What kind of eater are you?

scenes.title: Meeting Your Body
narration: Have you ever wondered how your body works while you play at the park?
Just like a bicycle has parts, your body has special pieces too.
Let us explore the parts that help Kabir run, jump, and think.

scenes.title: The Big Three
narration: First is the brain, which lives in your head and controls everything.
Next is the heart, which beats inside your chest like a drum.
Then we have the stomach, which turns your yummy lunch into energy.
These parts work together every single second without stopping.

scenes.title: Watching Them Work
narration: When Kabir runs, his brain tells his legs to move fast.
His heart pumps blood quickly to give his muscles strength.
After the race, his stomach digests a tasty banana for energy.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Your brain thinks, your heart pumps blood, and your stomach digests food.
Taking care of these parts helps you grow strong and healthy.
Think about it: which body part helps you feel the sun on your skin?

scenes.title: Look at the Animals
narration: Have you noticed how your pet dog has paws but a bird has wings?
Why do animals have such different body parts?
Let us explore how these parts help them live in their homes.

scenes.title: Parts for Survival
narration: A bird uses its wings to fly high above the mango trees.
A fish uses its fins to swim quickly through the river water.
An elephant uses its long trunk to drink water and grab snacks.
Each part is a special tool designed for a specific job.

scenes.title: A Special Example
narration: Think about a strong tiger living in the tall grass.
It has sharp claws to catch its food safely.
It also has soft pads on its paws to walk silently.
These parts work together perfectly for the tiger to hunt.

scenes.title: Recap and Reflect
narration: Animals have different parts to help them eat, move, and stay safe.
From wings to trunks, every single part has a big purpose.
If you could have any animal body part, which one would you choose?

scenes.title: A Lunchbox Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered why your body feels super energetic after a healthy lunch?
Just like a toy car needs batteries, your body needs the right fuel to play.
Let us see what makes your school tiffin truly powerful.

scenes.title: The Food Groups
narration: First, we have grains like rotis that give us energy to run and jump.
Next are proteins like dal and eggs which help your muscles grow big and strong.
Then we have fruits and vegetables filled with vitamins to keep us from getting sick.
Even a tiny bit of healthy fats helps our brain work its very best.

scenes.title: A Balanced Meal
narration: Imagine Rohan's plate with a round roti, a bowl of yellow dal, and crunchy carrots.
The roti gives him energy for his cricket match in the afternoon.
The dal helps his muscles recover, and the carrots keep his eyes bright.

scenes.title: Staying Healthy Always
narration: Remember, a mix of grains, proteins, and veggies makes the perfect meal.
Try to eat different colors on your plate to get all the healthy vitamins.
Think about it, what is your favorite vegetable and how does it help you grow?

scenes.title: The Toy Box Mystery
narration: Aarav is playing with his toy box and finds a squishy teddy and a hard building block.
Why is the teddy bear so soft but the block is so very hard?
Let us discover why materials feel different when we touch them.

scenes.title: Hard vs Soft Secrets
narration: Hard materials are strong and do not change shape when you push them.
Soft materials are gentle and change their shape easily when you squeeze them.
Think of a steel spoon for soup versus a soft cotton pillow.

scenes.title: Testing Our Toys
narration: Aarav presses his finger on a bouncy rubber ball.
The ball changes shape because it is soft, then pops back to round.
Now he taps his heavy wooden desk with a pencil.
The desk stays firm because it is a hard material.

scenes.title: Wrapping Up
narration: Hard things are tough and soft things are squishy to touch.
We use hard materials to build houses and soft ones for comfort.
Think about it: what is the softest thing you can find in your school bag?

scenes.title: Meet Your Super Senses
narration: Have you ever wondered how you know your lunch is ready before you see it?
We have five special body parts that help us explore the whole world.
Let us discover what each one does for you every single day.

scenes.title: How We See and Hear
narration: Your eyes help you see the bright sun and colorful flowers in the garden.
Your ears catch sounds like the chirping birds or the school bell ringing.
These senses send fast messages straight to your clever brain.

scenes.title: Taste, Touch, and Smell
narration: Imagine eating a spicy samosa, your tongue tastes the yummy flavor right away.
Your nose sniffs the sweet scent of jasmine flowers in the park.
Finally, your skin feels if a toy is soft or a stone is hard.

scenes.title: Recap and Big Idea
narration: Eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin are our five amazing sense organs.
They work together like a team to help us learn about everything.
Think about it, which sense do you use most when playing hide and seek?

scenes.title: Why Do We Get Sweaty
narration: Have you ever played cricket in the park and felt really hot and sweaty?
Your body works hard when you run, so it makes sweat to stay cool.
But sweat can make us feel sticky and bring germs that smell.

scenes.title: The Power of Moving
narration: Running and jumping makes your heart beat faster and your muscles strong.
Like Rohan playing tag, exercise helps you feel happy and full of energy.
Always remember to drink water after you play to stay hydrated.

scenes.title: Washing Away the Dirt
narration: After playtime, it is time to wash away the sweat and dirt.
Use soap to scrub your hands, under your arms, and your feet.
Putting on clean clothes helps you feel fresh and stops those smelly germs.

scenes.title: Stay Fresh and Fit
narration: Exercise keeps your body strong and bathing keeps your skin healthy.
Keep moving every day and always wash up when you are done.
Think about it: what is your favorite way to get moving today?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Shapes
narration: Aarav is eating a juicy mango, but his ice cube is melting in his lemonade.
Why does the ice stay a shape, but the juice flows everywhere?
Let us discover the secret world of solids and liquids together.

scenes.title: Understanding Solids and Liquids
narration: Solids are strong and keep their own shape, like your heavy school bag.
Liquids are different because they flow and take the shape of their container.
If you pour water into a round glass, it becomes a round shape.

scenes.title: Testing at Home
narration: Let us look at your kitchen cupboard, Aarav finds a hard steel spoon.
The spoon is a solid because it stays the same even in your hand.
Now pour water into a bowl; see how it fills the space perfectly?
The water is a liquid because it moves and flows easily.

scenes.title: Quick Wrap Up
narration: Solids have a fixed shape, but liquids flow to fit their container.
Everything around us is either a solid, liquid, or a gas.
Think about it: is the honey in your jar a solid or a liquid?

scenes.title: The Curious Shadow
narration: Have you noticed your shadow following you while you play at the park?
Why does it sometimes get long and sometimes hide under your feet?
Let us discover how light creates these dark shapes.

scenes.title: How Shadows Appear
narration: Light travels in a straight line from the sun or a bulb.
When an object blocks the light, it cannot pass through.
The dark space behind the object is what we call a shadow.

scenes.title: A Sunny Example
narration: Imagine Rohan standing under the bright morning sun.
His body stops the sunlight from hitting the ground behind him.
A dark shape appears on the grass exactly where the light is blocked.
When Rohan moves, his shadow moves with him too.

scenes.title: Quick Shadow Recap
narration: Light travels in lines and shadows happen when something blocks it.
Opaque objects like books make dark shadows, but clear glass does not.
Think about it: can you make a shadow without any light at all?

scenes.title: The Mystery of Movement
narration: Have you ever wondered how Rohan opens his heavy classroom door?
Or why he tugs his school bag along the floor?
Everything moves because of a special action called a force.

scenes.title: Push or Pull
narration: A push is when you move something away from your body.
Like when you kick a football across the park.
A pull is when you bring something closer to you.
Like pulling a heavy cart filled with juicy mangoes.

scenes.title: Seeing Forces in Action
narration: Let us watch Ananya play with her toy car.
She gives the car a gentle push to make it zoom forward.
Then she pulls the string to bring it back to her.
It changes direction because she applied a new force.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Forces
narration: Push moves things away and pull brings things closer.
Both are forces that help us move objects every single day.
Think about it: do you push or pull when you brush your teeth?

scenes.title: Feeling the World Around Us
narration: Arav is touching his soft teddy bear and his rough brick wall.
Have you ever wondered why some things feel bumpy and others feel silky?
Today we are exploring the secret of rough and smooth surfaces.

scenes.title: Understanding Texture
narration: Smooth things are flat and even, like the surface of a glass bowl.
Rough things have tiny bumps, ridges, or holes that you can feel.
When your skin rubs against these bumps, your brain knows it is rough.
Smooth things let your fingers slide easily without any catching.

scenes.title: Testing Objects at Home
narration: Let us check a shiny steel spoon from your kitchen.
Because it is flat and even, we call it smooth.
Now, feel a piece of sandpaper or a tree bark outside.
Those tiny bumps make your fingers feel a little scratchy.

scenes.title: Summary and Challenge
narration: Smooth things are flat, while rough things have bumps and ridges.
Your sense of touch helps you explore the world every single day.
Think about it: Can you find three rough things in your school bag?

scenes.title: The Invisible Air Around Us
narration: Look at the trees swaying in the park today.
Can you see what is pushing the leaves?
It is air, which is all around us, even if we cannot see it.

scenes.title: Where Water Hides
narration: Rohan drinks a cool glass of water after playing cricket.
Water is in our taps, in rivers, and even inside clouds.
Air and water are the two most important things for life.
Plants and animals need them to stay healthy and strong.

scenes.title: Making a Paper Boat
narration: Let us put a small paper boat in a bowl of water.
If you blow on it, the air makes the boat move.
The water holds the boat up while the air pushes it forward.

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Challenge
narration: Air is everywhere, and water helps everything grow.
We must keep our water clean and our air fresh.
Think about it: how can you help save water at home?

scenes.title: The Curious Summer Sun
narration: Have you noticed how hot it is when we play cricket in the park?
But in December, we wear sweaters to school. Why does the weather change?
Let's find out why the seasons dance around the year.

scenes.title: Earth Is Tilted
narration: Our Earth is like a spinning top that tilts a little to the side.
As Earth travels around the sun, different parts get more direct sunlight.
When your part of the Earth tilts toward the sun, it is summer.
When it tilts away, the days get cooler and it is winter.

scenes.title: A Year of Changes
narration: Think of a mango tree in a garden in India.
In summer, the sun helps the sweet mangoes grow big.
Then comes the monsoon rain to feed the thirsty ground.
Finally, winter comes and the tree rests before starting over.

scenes.title: Remembering Our Seasons
narration: Seasons happen because Earth is tilted while it orbits the sun.
This tilt gives us summer, winter, and everything in between.
Think about it: If Earth did not tilt, would we still have seasons?
